title: Shortest path visiting all nodes
statement: An undirected connected graph has n ≤ 12 nodes (adjacency lists). Return the length of the shortest walk that visits every node; you may start and end anywhere and revisit nodes and edges.
hints: A position alone isn't a state: you also need which nodes you've visited.
BFS over (node, mask), starting from every node at once.

solution.explanation: n ≤ 12 is the signal: a subset fits in an integer. The state (current node, visited set) has n·2ⁿ ≈ 50,000 values, and every move costs 1, so it's multi-source BFS from Part 4 on an enlarged state. Recognising "small n → bitmask state" is the whole problem.
